bug_description.normalized: The staged 23,346-byte `fuzzing::datasource::Datasource` witness chooses `decoder.init()`, then `set_ogg_serial_number(...)`, then `set_metadata_ignore(FLAC__METADATA_TYPE_STREAMINFO)` because the raw metadata selector byte is `0x20` and falls through the `default` arm of `Get<FLAC__MetadataType>()`, and then enters loop opcode `4` (`process_until_end_of_stream()`) at datasource offset 72. During the crashing decode, `read_frame_header_()` consumes attacker-controlled frame-header bytes and materializes `decoder->private_->frame.header.blocksize`. Later `read_subframe_()` selects the LPC subframe path, `read_subframe_lpc_()` accepts partitioned Rice residual coding under a guard that uses that attacker-controlled `blocksize`, and `read_residual_partitioned_rice_()` derives `partition_samples` and the residual count `u` from the same `blocksize` before calling `FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block()` with `rice_parameter > 0`. Once whole buffered words are exhausted and execution enters `process_tail`, the bitreader reloads `cwords = br->consumed_words` and unconditionally executes `b = br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits`. When `cwords` equals the 2048-word capacity of the 8192-byte buffer allocated by `FLAC__bitreader_init()`, that statement reads one word past the allocation and triggers the observed AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow at `src/libFLAC/bitreader.c:867`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that reads attacker-controlled frame-header bytes into parser state later used to decode the crashing frame's `blocksize`.
source.value_from: Offline parsing of the staged `poc` shows the datasource prelude selects `decoder.init()`, enables `set_ogg_serial_number(...)`, enables `set_metadata_ignore(FLAC__METADATA_TYPE_STREAMINFO)` because the raw selector byte is `0x20` and the `Get<FLAC__MetadataType>()` switch returns STREAMINFO through its `default` arm, and then enters loop opcode `4` (`process_until_end_of_stream()`) at byte offset 72. The exact post-offset-72 `GetData(0)` callback chunking is not preserved, but this statement is the first project-side read on the crashing path that materializes the frame-header bytes consumed by the downstream `blocksize` decode.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call packages the attacker-derived residual count `u` and current partition's Rice parameter into the exact arguments that drive the buggy tail decode in `FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: `partition_samples` is derived from the already-decoded `frame.header.blocksize` and `partition_order` at line 2753, `u` is derived from `partition_samples` and `predictor_order` at line 2772, and `rice_parameter` is read from attacker-controlled residual partition metadata at line 2767.

root_cause.description: The `process_tail` decoder reloads `cwords` from the bitreader state and dereferences `br->buffer[cwords]` without checking that the index is still below the allocated bitreader capacity.
root_cause.note: The fixed patch changes this exact statement to `cwords < br->capacity ? br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits : 0`, which is the missing obligation on the vulnerable path.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The 32-bit load from `br->buffer[cwords]` reads one word past the end of the 2048-word / 8192-byte bitreader allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 4` at this line on address `0x625000002100`, exactly 0 bytes to the right of the region allocated by `FLAC__bitreader_init()` at `src/libFLAC/bitreader.c:268`.

parser_admitted.description: The datasource-selected `process_until_end_of_stream()` run has already passed stream initialization and frame sync, and `read_frame_()` has entered FLAC frame-header parsing for the candidate crashing frame.

coarse_trace.summary: Offline parsing of the first 72 datasource bytes shows the harness chooses `decoder.init()`, then `set_ogg_serial_number(...)`, then `set_metadata_ignore(STREAMINFO)` because raw selector byte `0x20` falls through the `default` arm of `Get<FLAC__MetadataType>()`, and then `process_until_end_of_stream()`. Subsequent datasource records are consumed through libFLAC callbacks while decoding the crashing stream, but the exact callback chunking is not preserved.
Frame-header parsing reads attacker-controlled header bytes and materializes `frame.header.blocksize`, which later governs the partition-order guard and residual-count arithmetic.
Subframe parsing reads the current subframe header and selects `read_subframe_lpc_()` with an attacker-derived LPC predictor order.
The LPC parser reads the entropy-coding method and partition order, and the `frame.header.blocksize >> partition_order < order` guard does not reject the partitioned-Rice path.

Residual parsing reads the current partition's Rice parameter, derives `partition_samples` and `u` from the attacker-controlled blocksize and predictor order, and calls `FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block()`.

With `parameter > 0`, the bitreader eventually enters `process_tail` after whole words are exhausted, reloads `cwords` from the consumed state, and reads `br->buffer[cwords]` without a capacity check, causing the saved heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Over the two loop iterations at line 2203, this statement reads the next attacker-controlled frame-header bytes and stores them into `raw_header[2]` and `raw_header[3]`. Those bytes carry the blocksize code later decoded for the crashing frame.

The attacker-controlled blocksize code in `raw_header[2] >> 4` is decoded here. It either maps directly to one of the fixed blocksize assignments at lines 2222, 2228, or 2242, or it selects `blocksize_hint`, in which case lines 2392-2403 read one or two more attacker-controlled header bytes and assign `decoder->private_->frame.header.blocksize = x+1`. The staged artifacts do not preserve which of those source-level assignments produced the crashing frame's size, but one of them materializes the `blocksize` later consumed by the guard and `u` arithmetic below.
Reads the attacker-controlled subframe header byte for the same frame after the header parser has already materialized `decoder->private_->frame.header.blocksize`.

After masking the wasted-bits flag and bypassing the earlier subframe cases, the attacker-controlled header selects the LPC decoder. The same byte is transformed into LPC predictor order `((x >> 1) & 31) + 1` for the downstream residual decode.

The LPC parser reads the entropy-coding method and partition order from attacker-controlled bits. On the crashing path the method is partitioned Rice (or Rice2), and the guard `decoder->private_->frame.header.blocksize >> u32 < order` does not reject the attacker-chosen partition order, so residual decoding continues with the previously decoded `blocksize`.
For the current residual partition, the decoder reads the attacker-controlled Rice parameter that determines how each residual symbol will be split into unary MSBs and binary LSBs in the bitreader.

fine_trace.code: const uint32_t partition_samples = partition_order > 0? decoder->private_->frame.header.blocksize >> partition_order : decoder->private_->frame.header.blocksize - predictor_order;
fine_trace.note: Using the attacker-controlled `decoder->private_->frame.header.blocksize` and the accepted partition order, the decoder derives `partition_samples`, the per-partition sample count that feeds the current partition's residual count `u`.

Because `rice_parameter < pesc`, the decoder stays on the Rice-coded branch instead of switching to the raw-bits escape path. It derives the current partition's residual count `u` from `partition_samples` and predictor order, then passes both `u` and `rice_parameter` into `FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block()`.

The crash occurs past line 776, so the `parameter == 0` special-case decoder is not taken on the crashing call. The attacker-controlled Rice parameter is therefore nonzero, and execution stays on the tail-handling logic that contains the buggy read.

The buggy line sits inside `process_tail`. Control reaches that body once no whole buffered word remains: either immediately via `if(cwords >= words)` or after the fast loop jumps through `incomplete_msbs` / `incomplete_lsbs` when it runs out of words. The saved static artifacts establish this exhausted-buffer tail path, not the bottom `val < end` condition, as the real control edge into the crashing body.

Inside `process_tail`, helper reads consume the unary MSBs and binary LSBs for another Rice-coded value, then lines 864-866 reload the updated word index from the bitreader state. `FLAC__bitreader_init()` set `br->capacity = 65536u / FLAC__BITS_PER_WORD` at line 267 and `FLAC__BITS_PER_WORD` is 32 on this build, so the buffer holds 2048 words / 8192 bytes; the saved ASan address shows the crashing reload has `cwords == br->capacity == 2048`.

Root cause. After reloading `cwords`, the tail decoder immediately indexes `br->buffer[cwords]` without checking `cwords < br->capacity`. The patch adds exactly that guard and substitutes `0` when the reloaded index is already at capacity.

Sink. With `cwords == 2048`, this statement performs a 4-byte read from `br->buffer[2048]`, one 32-bit word past the 2048-word / 8192-byte allocation from `FLAC__bitreader_init()`. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow here with stack `FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block -> read_residual_partitioned_rice_ -> read_subframe_lpc_`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The only staged patch hunk changes the crashing statement to `cwords < br->capacity ? br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits : 0`, directly guarding the out-of-bounds read at `src/libFLAC/bitreader.c:867`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_17069-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which replayed the staged `poc` against `/out/fuzzer_decoder` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` in `FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block`.

format.name: fuzzing::datasource::Datasource stream for fuzzer_decoder
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 23,346-byte `fuzzing::datasource::Datasource` witness in `gt_results/arvo_17069/poc`. Offline parsing of its first 72 bytes shows `Get<bool>()` selects `decoder.init()`, later enables `set_ogg_serial_number(...)`, enables `set_metadata_ignore(FLAC__METADATA_TYPE_STREAMINFO)` because raw selector byte `0x20` falls through the `default` arm of `Get<FLAC__MetadataType>()`, and then starts the loop with opcode `4` (`process_until_end_of_stream()`). After that point the remaining datasource records are consumed through libFLAC callbacks, and the saved artifacts do not preserve the exact post-offset-72 `GetData(0)` chunk boundaries between read, write, and seek callback uses. To hit the saved crash, those callback-driven records must still let `read_frame_header_()` materialize the crashing frame's `blocksize`, `read_subframe_()` select the LPC path, `read_subframe_lpc_()` accept partitioned-Rice entropy coding, `read_residual_partitioned_rice_()` take the `rice_parameter < pesc` branch, and `FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block()` bypass the `parameter == 0` return and enter `process_tail` after whole buffered words are exhausted, so line 867 performs the observed 4-byte read when `cwords == br->capacity == 2048`. This contract is intentionally limited to witnesses that recreate that same callback-driven parser state; the staged artifacts do not support a broader claim about datasource chunking or neighboring inputs.
